# Browser-Local Architecture

## Runtime Ownership

The deployed product is a single static page. Vite builds `front/` into root
`dist/`. The browser runs React and the pure conversion modules; no service,
remote account API, Pages Function, Worker, database or server-side session
participates. `vendor/` contains pinned Git submodules for source evidence and is
neither built nor served. Recursive checkout retrieves the original source from
its owners instead of copying upstream OAuth constants into the parent history.

`src/conversion/` owns parsing, provider mapping, safe names, validation, bundle
generation and ZIP generation. `front/src/App.tsx` owns import state, selection,
preview visibility, filtering, downloads and operator notices. No router or
global state library is needed for this one workspace.

## Data Flow

File input, directory selection, drag/drop and paste become `InputSource[]` in
React memory. Conversion validates bounded JSON then processes accounts in input
order. Each attempted account becomes an entry or an explicit issue. Valid
accounts can be selected individually. Failed accounts never become exports.
Downloads use user-triggered Blob URLs; temporary URLs are revoked afterward.

Selecting files appends to the current file batch. Pasted documents are added at
conversion time. Direction, source text and setting changes invalidate previous
results. Clear also invalidates pending asynchronous file reads with a generation
counter. Direction switching preserves input but discards previous results.

## Persistence And Privacy

Only the versioned preference key `cpa2sub2api:preferences:v1` is persisted. Its
allowlist contains exactly `concurrency` and `priority`; invalid or unavailable
storage falls back to defaults and does not block conversion. The application
does not persist source/result JSON or use IndexedDB, service workers or URLs
for account data. Reloading clears application input/result state.

Preview token fields are recursively masked by default. Displaying real tokens
requires an explicit checkbox; copying respects that state. Downloads always
contain real credentials, independently of masking. Masking is not a guarantee
that arbitrary metadata or email addresses are anonymized. Input is untrusted;
React text escaping and generic parser errors prevent HTML execution and raw
JSON snippets in error messages. JWT payload decoding is best-effort metadata
extraction, never signature verification or authentication.

Static production responses apply `_headers`, including a CSP with no network
connections, remote scripts, inline scripts, embedding or forms. This is defense
in depth, not protection from browser extensions, compromised dependencies,
clipboard history, local downloads or browser-managed recovery. Cloudflare
analytics/script injection must remain disabled. Vite HMR is development-only
and is not covered by production network guarantees.

## Verification

Unit tests isolate conversion and preference storage. Browser tests use compiled
production assets with the production CSP attached to document responses. They
check actual JSON/ZIP downloads, reload clearing, masked/revealed previews and
runtime request origins. A separate local Pages emulator verifies actual static
headers. Neither test implies live deployment or live account validity.

# Deploy Static Assets To Cloudflare Pages

## Local Build And Emulation

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm check
pnpm verify:dist
pnpm pages:dev
```

The project-local pinned Wrangler reads `wrangler.jsonc`, serves `dist/` and
applies Pages `_headers` locally. It binds loopback; it does not deploy or require
an account mutation. Do not use Vite preview to prove Pages header processing:
Vite serves `_headers` as a file rather than interpreting it.

## Git Integration

The deployed project uses Direct Upload with no Git integration; pushes to
GitHub do not trigger a deployment. This section applies to a separate
Git-integrated project. A Direct Upload project cannot be switched to Git
integration in place.

After explicitly authorizing creation/publication of the Git remote, connect it
through Cloudflare Workers & Pages → Create application → Pages → Import an
existing Git repository. Use repository root, production branch `main`, build
command `pnpm build` and output `dist`. Set `NODE_VERSION=22.19.0` or a newer
compatible version and `PNPM_VERSION=12.10.1`; use the current Pages build image.
The vendor package managers and vendor Go modules must not be executed.
The Vite build needs no initialized vendor submodules. Source-backed tests and
`pnpm check` require `git submodule update --init --recursive` in environments
that do not clone submodules automatically.

For reproducible explicit dependency installation, Pages also supports
`SKIP_DEPENDENCY_INSTALL=1` with the build command
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`. Do not put account credentials,
OAuth tokens or input files in build environment variables or repository files.

## Direct Upload

Only after the owner authorizes a target Cloudflare account/project, check the
local Wrangler version/help and provide its API token privately to the process.
`pnpm pages:deploy` builds and verifies dist/ before invoking the portable
deployment helper. The helper pins the selected account, project cpa2sub2api
and production branch main. This invokes a real remote upload; do not treat it
as a dry run or part of routine local verification. Project creation, custom
domains and account settings are separate external actions.

The owner selected the Cloudflare account associated with `momoe.org`.
`scripts/pages-deploy.mjs` pins account ID `d7bf5987a206b7ea342add617a9d9dcd`
through the deployment process environment; Pages rejects `account_id` in
`wrangler.jsonc`, even though the generic Wrangler schema includes it.
The account ID is not a credential. Keep API tokens outside the repository and
use credentials scoped to this account rather than relying on an ambient token
for another account. Read-only API checks confirmed account access before
creation; project creation and the successful upload then proved the write path.

## Verified Production Deployment

The owner explicitly authorized project creation and deployment on 2026-10-16.

| Property | Verified value |
| --- | --- |
| Project | cpa2sub2api |
| Production URL | https://cpa2sub2api-e3k.pages.dev/ |
| Deployment URL | https://a6d1a8e3.cpa2sub2api-e3k.pages.dev/ |
| Deployment ID | a6d1a8e3-bc1b-412d-a319-20fbd021b37e |
| Deployment source commit | f00a365c0b48380fb9a8e75f0cf270c79585e7a0 |
| Production branch | main |
| Completed | 2026-10-16T12:55:04Z |
| API deployment status | success |
| Git integration / Functions / Web Analytics tag | none / false / none |

HTTPS document, JS and CSS responses matched dist/ byte for byte. Actual
response headers supplied the local-only CSP and other configured security
headers. An unmodified production page passed Chromium checks for four-provider
forward and reverse conversion, masked previews, unsupported-account isolation,
individual/merged JSON and reverse ZIP downloads, no credential persistence,
reload clearing and a 390px layout. No external runtime requests or page errors
occurred. A hostile external fetch was blocked by the actual connect-src CSP.
Desktop/mobile screenshots are ignored local artifacts in test-results/.

The Git remote remains https://github.com/furedericca-lab/cpa2sub2api. No custom
domain, momoe.org DNS, Git integration, analytics, backend or unrelated account
setting was configured. Only synthetic account data was used for acceptance;
live provider OAuth acceptance was not tested.

## Post-Deployment Acceptance

1. Confirm the document and versioned JS/CSS assets load over HTTPS.
2. Check response CSP includes `connect-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`,
   `object-src 'none'`, and self-only script/style sources; verify no inline or
   external runtime scripts are injected.
3. Keep Cloudflare Web Analytics and automatic third-party script injection off.
   Strict CSP may block such scripts, but do not rely on blocking alone.
4. In browser developer tools, convert synthetic data and prove that no account
   API, remote font, analytics request or upload occurs. Verify JSON and ZIP
   downloads and that reloading clears input/results.
5. Ensure only built assets are published: no vendor sources, raw input, tests,
   private files, source maps, Functions or `_worker.js`.

Cloudflare Pages parses `_headers` for static responses; those rules do not
protect future Pages Functions. Adding a backend changes the privacy contract
and requires a separate design. This site needs no SPA redirects for nested
routes because it has only a root workspace.

## Official References Checked

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/framework-guides/deploy-a-react-site/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/build-image/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/headers/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/functions/wrangler-configuration/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/get-started/direct-upload/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/pages/subresources/projects/methods/create/

Current documentation was retrieved during implementation/deployment. Repeat
the post-deployment acceptance checks after future uploads; the evidence above
describes the initial production deployment rather than all future versions.

# Maintain Pinned Vendor Submodules

## Ownership

`vendor/sub2api` and `vendor/CLIProxyAPI` are complete pinned Git submodules of
the public upstreams. They have no root workspace membership or runtime startup.
Root `pnpm install/build` processes only the converter. Keep both projects'
original dotfiles and license texts intact. The parent Git tree stores only
gitlinks, not copies of upstream OAuth client constants. Initial inline-vendor
publication was blocked by GitHub push protection; the repair deliberately used
submodules rather than bypassing protection or editing upstream source.

`vendor/vendor-lock.json` records each URL, full commit, file count and SHA-256
aggregate. The aggregate hashes sorted relative paths plus each file's content
hash, excluding `.git` metadata. Verification checks both the initialized
submodule HEAD and content digest. It does not establish upstream authenticity,
Git executable-bit parity or third-party security. Recorded commits pin the
inspected format evidence even if upstream later changes.

## Verification

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
pnpm verify:vendor
git submodule status
```

Fresh clones should use `git clone --recurse-submodules`. Source-backed unit tests
and `pnpm check` require initialized vendors, but `pnpm build` does not. Parent
`git ls-tree HEAD vendor/sub2api vendor/CLIProxyAPI` must show mode `160000`.
Never force-add source files from inside a vendor into the parent repository.

## Authorized Refresh

1. Confirm the worktree and explicit vendor-refresh scope. Preserve unrelated
   edits; do not overwrite modified vendor trees.
2. Fetch the authorized public upstream in its submodule and record the exact
   intended commit. Review changes to credential types and data import/export.
3. With the submodule worktree clean, check out that exact commit detached. Do
   not follow floating branch HEAD or overwrite unrelated local vendor edits.
4. Adapt application mappings and synthetic tests for any accepted format changes.
5. From the root, run `node scripts/vendor.mjs record vendor` for the selected
   submodule HEADs. Review `.gitmodules`, parent gitlinks and the manifest together;
   recording a digest alone does not authorize a pin change.
6. Run `pnpm check`, `pnpm verify:dist`, and affected browser acceptance. Update
   mapping notes, provenance and maintenance evidence. Stage the submodule
   gitlinks and manifest, inspect the diff and publish only when requested.

Do not fix application behavior by editing vendor source. A vendor update is
separate from a routine converter UI/core change and never requires running
the vendor services or introducing their secrets into this repository.

# Conversion Contract And Compatibility

## Canonical Format Evidence

Pinned source versions are in `vendor/vendor-lock.json`.

- `vendor/sub2api/backend/internal/handler/admin/account_data.go`:
  `DataPayload`, `DataAccount`, `validateDataHeader`, `validateDataAccount`.
- `vendor/CLIProxyAPI/internal/auth/codex/token.go`: `CodexTokenStorage`.
- `vendor/CLIProxyAPI/internal/auth/claude/token.go`: `ClaudeTokenStorage`.
- `vendor/CLIProxyAPI/sdk/auth/antigravity.go`: `BuildAntigravityAuth`.
- The reference project's `docs/src/converter.mjs` supplies the Gemini nested
  token mapping and four-provider workflow; reference commit is in THIRD_PARTY.

This is source/schema compatibility, not live acceptance by an authenticated
running service. The tool does not log in, probe endpoints, validate signatures,
refresh credentials, or prove that a provider will accept a converted account.

## Mapping Matrix

| CPA type | sub2api platform | Primary mapped fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codex` | `openai` | access/refresh/id tokens, account/user/organization IDs, email, plan, expiry |
| `claude` | `anthropic` | access/refresh/id tokens, email_address, account/organization UUIDs, expiry |
| `gemini` | `gemini` | nested token access/refresh, expiry, scopes, token type, project ID, email |
| `antigravity` | `antigravity` | access/refresh, project ID, token type, plan, email, expiry |

Forward output has `type: sub2api-data`, `version: 1`, UTC `exported_at`,
`proxies: []` and `accounts`. Each account uses `type: oauth`, concurrency `10`
and priority `1` unless edited. OpenAI expiry is ISO text; the other providers
use Unix-second strings in credentials, matching the reference convention and
sub2api's flexible credential-time parser.

Reverse input accepts an accounts envelope, account array or a single account.
Version 1, legacy `sub2api-bundle` and unversioned envelopes are accepted.
Unknown explicit document types/versions are rejected. An account must explicitly
be `type: oauth`; absent type is not guessed. Missing CPA provider type is also
rejected instead of guessing Codex.

Reverse output produces one native CPA JSON per valid account. OpenAI maps to
`type: codex`, Anthropic to `type: claude`. Gemini recreates the nested `token`
object. Codex emits an empty `refresh_token` string if missing, preserving the
reference behavior. Other unavailable fields are omitted, not invented.

## Expiry And Validation

Expiry accepts ISO text, Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds and numeric strings.
Explicit timestamps take precedence over decoded token claims. Antigravity can
derive an absolute expiry from its recorded timestamp plus `expires_in`.
An unanchored relative lifetime is not added to the current clock: doing that
could falsely extend old credentials. Invalid timestamps are omitted with a
warning; expired tokens remain exportable with a warning. Opaque access tokens
are allowed. Missing access tokens and recognizable masked access tokens fail.
Missing refresh tokens and Google project IDs produce warnings where applicable.

JSON input is bounded to 500 files, 20 MiB total, 5000 accounts and 64 nested
levels. It supports BOM, arrays, JSONL and adjacent documents. A malformed source
file is rejected without exposing parser excerpts; other source files continue.
Account errors are isolated within otherwise valid documents. Oversized account
documents fail without silently accepting their first 5000 records.

## Deliberate Non-Parity

API-key, setup-token, upstream, unsupported-provider and active SIWC credentials
are not converted. Groups, status, billing, scheduling, proxy bindings and
service configuration are not portable OAuth credential fields. Reverse entries
always warn about sub2api operational settings. CPA disabled/proxy_url metadata
gets an explicit forward warning and never becomes active sub2api configuration.

Unknown CPA top-level fields are retained under
`extra.cpa2sub2api = { version: 1, provider, metadata }`. This preserves such
fields as prefix, custom flags and Claude device IDs if sub2api retains the
metadata. Mapped credential keys are never restored from this archive; current
credentials remain authoritative. Unknown nested Gemini token fields, arbitrary
sub2api credentials/extra, exact original timestamps and filename spelling are
not guaranteed to round trip. Do not describe the tool as a complete backup.

Duplicate accounts are not deduplicated. Safe Unicode filenames are flattened
and bounded; case-insensitive collisions receive numeric suffixes. ZIP contents
are per-account JSON with those same names. A masked preview is never the source
of downloadable credentials.
